verdicts.evidence: Real experiments on a synthetic DGP (n=4000, 8 reps) show IBS bias ranging from −0.0795 under administrative censoring to ~0.000 under covariate-dependent censoring at 80%, and C-index bias increasing monotonically with censoring rate, directly demonstrating mechanism- and rate-dependent distortions — but only 2 metric families are tested on fully synthetic data with no real clinical datasets or full model panel.

Near-tied model ranking agreement with the oracle drops from 100% at 0% censoring to 29–42% at 80% across mechanisms (24 reps), directly showing unreliable model comparison under heavy censoring, while widely-separated models retain 100% agreement — but this is on the same reduced synthetic setup with only C-index and 4 fixed risk scores.

overall: The logbook provides real, executed experiments with concrete numbers that directionally support both claims, but on a clearly reduced synthetic setup (no real clinical data, subset of metrics and models) rather than the paper's semi-synthetic design on PBC/FLCHAIN/METABRIC with a full model panel.
